$comment: Hand-kept (NSP-009 §2): a picker node that owes no spec, with the reason. Read by scripts/node-spec/census.js, which fails on a name that is not a picker node or an entry with no reason, and prints every exemption — never hidden.

Component Children.reason: Not a node: the runtime never makes one — nodescope.ts createNodeFromModel returns before createNode, after telling the owning component instance which node is its child root (setChildRoot). It has no ports, no state and nothing on the wire; what it does is where a component instance's children are placed, a graph rule.
Component Children.ruled: Richard, 2026-10-08 (README §7): count it as done, with the reason written down
Component Children.graded: its placement, by a graph scenario once the graph runner places children (NSP-008)

CSS Definition.reason: Web-only by nature: it has no outputs and nothing on the wire; what it does is add its Style text to the page's head as a <style> element for as long as a node with its id exists (ref-counted per node id, css-definition.ts), replace it when Style changes, and remove it with the last one. That is a page effect of the browser, not a behaviour a reducer can state.
CSS Definition.ruled: Richard, 2026-10-09 (README R17): leave it out — exempt as web-only, rather than spec the stylesheet on the page
CSS Definition.graded: nothing — an export or a new runtime that drops the CSS is not caught by the node-spec suite; the templates' look is graded where they are drawn
